name: Flex PCB

claims.claim_text: Flexible circuit boards carried a substantial cost premium over rigid boards in the early 2010s, enough that engineers treated a flex build as an expensive choice rather than a default one.
claims.quote_verbatim: but it is expensive. Like really expensive. As in a flex board.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A common flex construction places several small rigid board islands along a single flexible circuit that runs continuously between them, so the flex itself acts as the interconnect.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was like tiny boards and then like a flex connector all the way through it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Mounting components directly onto flexible substrates is not a recent technique; flex boards with parts populated on them appear in consumer products from the 1970s and 1980s, such as Polaroid cameras.
claims.quote_verbatim: They would actually have the components mounted directly on the flex. It's not new technology. It's, it's many decades old.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Flex circuits are used in compact consumer products because routing a circuit around internal corners is often the only way to fit the electronics into the required form factor.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's the only way to package electronics inside these sorts of products, these sorts of consumer products. To get around corners and such. To actually meet the form factors.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Layers of polyimide in a flex circuit are joined with a bond film rather than liquid adhesive: a thin sheet of adhesive handled like tissue paper that melts and bonds the stack when heated and collapsed in a press.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's like a tissue paper, but it's glue. And then when you heat it up in a press and, and collapse it, it basically melts and bonds.
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: Flex-circuit bond film can be purchased either pre-applied to polyimide or as a standalone sheet, which allows a designer to build arbitrary multi-layer sandwiches of dissimilar materials such as carbon fiber and polyimide.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you had two pieces of capton for a flex circuit, you got to stick them together and you don't, you don't actually glue them together
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: Laminating stiff carbon-fibre layers around a polyimide core and then laser-cutting the carbon away in selected regions produces a mechanical flex hinge using the same construction principle as a flex circuit.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you cut away the carbon in the right spots, you could actually have a flex hinge, just like a flex circuit
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: For scale in laser-machined flex and polyimide work, 25 microns equals one thousandth of an inch and a human hair is roughly three thousandths of an inch, or 75 microns; production features of that era ran in the 100 to 200 micron range with two to five micron machine accuracy.
claims.quote_verbatim: 25 microns is a thousandth of an inch. And then a human hair would be, um, uh, three, three thousandths of an inch or 75 micron.
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: Conductive traces printed onto fabric or paper have far higher resistance than etched copper, on the order of a couple of ohms per inch, which restricts them to low-current sensor and battery-scale signals rather than power distribution.
claims.quote_verbatim: these are higher impedance traces, right? So these are not going to be like, you know, two ounce copper.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: CAD courses and cross platform creation - Printing Propaedeutic Patterns

claims.claim_text: Additive printing of circuits is a rastered, line-by-line deposition process whose time scales with the total area covered, which keeps it in the prototype and one-off niche rather than batch production.
claims.quote_verbatim: this is going to be, like, a rastered type of, of process where you have to print line by line
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: CAD courses and cross platform creation - Printing Propaedeutic Patterns

claims.claim_text: Hearing-aid electronics are typically built as three stacked dies covering DSP, analog and memory, all bonded down to a small flex print that also carries the microphones.
claims.quote_verbatim: everything bolted down to a small flex print
claims.speaker: Jørgen Jakobsen

claims.claim_text: A very thin board made from bare prepreg can be taped to a sheet of standard FR4 with polyimide tape and then run through normal pick-and-place and reflow, because prepreg lies flat instead of curling.
claims.quote_verbatim: literally you can just tape it down to a bit of standard FR4 with capstone tape, pick and place and reflow it as if it was an ordinary PCB
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Assembling on polyimide flex generally demands a vacuum bed or similar fixturing because the material curls and takes on tension; a prepreg-based thin board avoids that because it wants to stay flat.
claims.quote_verbatim: You don't have to use a vacuum bed or anything exotic like that because it wants to stay flat.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Board houses stock prepreg for building up multilayer boards, but few will supply it as a finished single-layer board, so sourcing thin flexible prepreg boards means finding the rare fabricator willing to do it.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got to find a manufacturer who's willing to just give you that pre-prig as a finished board
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Flexible printed circuit fabrication requires machined steel tools to stamp the coverlay, so each FPC design carries hard tooling that the factory shelves and reuses much like an injection-mould tool.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you get into FPC, you start making, um, steel tools to stamp the, the cap on
claims.speaker: Scotty Allen

claims.claim_text: A BGA placed on a flex circuit with no stiffener under it can be inspected optically without X-ray, because the polyimide substrate is translucent and the ball array is visible through the back of the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you put a BGA on a flex PCB, uh, with no stiffener, you can look through the back of the, uh, the FPC because it's clear and you can actually see all the balls
claims.speaker: Scotty Allen

claims.claim_text: The 0.4 mm pitch CPU BGAs used in iPhones sit at the difficult end of rework; experienced repair technicians reach a working result within a couple of attempts rather than first time every time.
claims.quote_verbatim: the 0.4 millimeter, um, CPU BGA is for the, for the iPhones are tricky
claims.speaker: Scotty Allen

claims.claim_text: A flex PCB is essentially copper laminated onto a plastic film, and ordering one from a board house remains the default route for a conforming circuit unless same-hour turnaround is needed.
claims.quote_verbatim: a flex PCB, which is copper on plastic
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Flex boards remained a cost premium over rigid FR4 into the late 2010s, which is what leaves room for lower-cost conformal circuit processes at the low end.
claims.quote_verbatim: flex are still somewhat expensive

claims.claim_text: Flex layer counts in consumer devices range widely: a lightning-to-audio connector assembly may use four to six layers, while an iPad processor flex can reach twelve layers and still bend, and two-layer flex behaves like a sheet of paper.
claims.quote_verbatim: Four or six-layer, rather, was a connector one inside, like, a lightning connector or lightning to audio connector.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Much of the flex circuitry in production equipment is not a standalone flex board but rigid-flex, where flexible layers sandwiched into the inner layers of the stackup join two rigid boards that then fold onto each other.
claims.quote_verbatim: Maybe the majority of flex technology out there is actually as interconnects between rigid boards.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Rigid-flex removes the cost and the reliability exposure of the connector-plus-ribbon-cable pair it replaces, since the interconnect becomes part of the board stackup rather than a mated assembly.
claims.quote_verbatim: Without having the expense of an extra connector and ribbon cable
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Populating components directly onto flex is harder than populating a rigid board, since pick-and-place and reflow assume a stiff, flat panel and flex generally needs a stiffener or carrier beneath it.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's always going to be easier to pick and place and reflow a rigid board
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: At 2.4 GHz and above a positional shift of one millimetre materially changes antenna behaviour, so an antenna carried on a flexible substrate that can move is less stable than one fixed to a rigid structure.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you are on high-frequency microwaves like 2.4 gigahertz or higher, then one millimeter is a lot
claims.speaker: Andreas Spiess

claims.claim_text: A degraded antenna can lose around half the radiated RF power, which shows up either as lost range or as shortened battery life once transmit power is raised to compensate.
claims.quote_verbatim: If your antenna is bad, you can easily, very, very fast, lose 50% of your RF power.
claims.speaker: Andreas Spiess

claims.claim_text: Circuitry patterned directly onto an injection-moulded housing costs more per unit than flex, so it suits small high-margin products such as hearing aids and payment terminals where internal volume is the binding constraint.
claims.quote_verbatim: for example, hearing aids. You can imagine these are very small and you do not want to lose a lot of space there
claims.speaker: Andreas Spiess

claims.claim_text: Building a sensing electrode array on a single flex circuit fixes the spacing between electrodes, and that known geometry is what allows an accurate tomographic image reconstruction.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can control the spacing between the electrodes, which can help you with image reconstruction because you just need that, uh, geometry knowledge
claims.speaker: Jean Rintoul

claims.claim_text: Flex PCB has been used as the substrate for a polymer banknote-style token, printed in full colour with an RFID chip embedded in the flexible material.
claims.quote_verbatim: It is a physical polymer type note, but it's actually a flex PCB.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: For very small flex boards the tooling charge dominates the quote, so ordering ten and ordering a hundred cost effectively the same, with the price stepping up only at the next panel bracket.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's no difference between ordering 10 and ordering a hundred
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Early flex construction was cruder, with the flexible material applied as a bottom layer, whereas modern rigid-flex embeds the flexible layers within the board stackup.
claims.quote_verbatim: they just stick it on the bottom and stick it as, as a bottom layer
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Designing and ordering a plain single-piece flex board differs from a rigid board mainly in the stackup specified to the fabricator, for example a 0.1 mm flex board in place of 1.6 mm fiberglass.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'll give you a 0.1 millimeter flex board instead of a 1.6 millimeter fiberglass
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The design and fabrication complexity of flex rises sharply only when flexible layers are combined into a rigid stackup; a standalone flex board is close to an ordinary board order.
claims.quote_verbatim: it only gets more complicated when you want to combine the flex into the rigid layers
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Planar motors can be built by etching the drive coil into a flex PCB and energising it with a driver; a haptic motor driver intended for phone vibration motors can substitute for a discrete H-bridge in this role.
claims.quote_verbatim: he's got a flex PCB with a coil in it and he drives current through it with motor drivers, but he found a new chip for it instead of, instead of using a, uh, an actual H bridge
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: When an expensive board built on controlled-impedance material cannot be re-spun, a flex overlay can carry a rework connection between distant points on the board in place of loose mod wires.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can make this big flex, you know, overlay kind of thing that joins up the two things. So you don't have to do mod wires
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A flex board designed to be folded into a three-dimensional assembly pushes cost into labour: operators must be trained to fold the panel in a fixed sequence and tack it with solder so it holds its folded shape.
claims.quote_verbatim: we were training these people at the factory to like fold it in the right order
claims.speaker: Akbar Dhanaliwala
claims.episode_title: Firmware Deployment and Troubleshooting with Akbar Dhanaliwala

claims.claim_text: Budgeting only a single board spin on a first flex design is a recognised risk, because flex introduces mechanical and folding variables that a first prototype rarely resolves.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you are working on flex, obviously don't, you know, don't just do one spin
claims.speaker: Joe Grand
claims.episode_title: New Life Skills with Joe Grand

claims.claim_text: Cutting a trace to patch a flex board is far harder than on rigid FR4, because the substrate is very thin and traces on the opposite layer sit directly beneath the cut.
claims.quote_verbatim: cutting a trace on a flex board is hard, right? Because there was traces on the other side and the substrate was super thin
claims.speaker: Joe Grand
claims.episode_title: New Life Skills with Joe Grand

claims.claim_text: Where a flex tail must fold to position a display in a head-mounted assembly, the fold path is worked out during board layout, and the layout is kept deliberately open-ended so mechanical revisions do not force a board re-spin.
claims.quote_verbatim: how the flex is going to need to be folded to put the display in that correct orientation, but I'm also trying to keep it as open-ended as possible
claims.speaker: Aedan Cullen
claims.episode_title: Building AR Headsets with Aedan Cullen

claims.claim_text: A folding flex actuator can be built from a single flexible PCB with three aluminium stiffeners that both fold the board into shape and form a pocket for the magnet the etched coil acts against.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's basically, one flexible PCB, that have, aluminium stiffeners, okay, it has two aluminium, three sorry, which, fold, which then, folds the PCB together, has a pocket, for a magnet
claims.speaker: Carl Bugeja
claims.episode_title: Motors on PCBs with Carl Bugeja

claims.claim_text: Choosing flex over rigid FR4 is often justified by eliminating discrete wires, since hand-soldering wires does not scale once hundreds of units are produced.
claims.quote_verbatim: consider producing, hundreds of, of this thing, soldering wires, one by one
claims.speaker: Carl Bugeja
claims.episode_title: Motors on PCBs with Carl Bugeja

claims.claim_text: Final test of a flex assembly should confirm the board has not been folded or bent in the wrong manner, since an incorrect fold is a defect the electrical test alone will not catch.
claims.quote_verbatim: make sure that for example, the flexible PCB is not, um, banded, like, like folded, for example, in the wrong manner
claims.speaker: Carl Bugeja
claims.episode_title: Motors on PCBs with Carl Bugeja

claims.claim_text: Flexible PCB pricing fell substantially over the 2010s, moving flex from an unaffordable option for hobby and student projects to a routinely orderable one.
claims.quote_verbatim: now they're much cheaper than, than what they were before
claims.speaker: Carl Bugeja
claims.episode_title: Motors on PCBs with Carl Bugeja

claims.claim_text: A flat flexible cable is a polyimide interconnect, whereas a flexible printed circuit board is a genuine custom PCB that can take any outline and may terminate in a tail that resembles an FFC.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's the flexible PC boards, which are really PC boards. They're custom PC boards, and they can take any shape. And sometimes they have a tail, and the tail may look like an FFC
claims.speaker: Davide Andrea
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea

claims.claim_text: A conductive ink circuit resembles a flexible printed circuit but is drawn with conductive ink rather than etched copper; microwave oven keypads use one, ending in a flexible tail that plugs into an FFC connector.
claims.quote_verbatim: the CIC, which is the conductive ink circuit, which looks like an FFC, flexible printed circuit. But it's done by drawing the circuit with ink. And you will, for example, find it in the keypad for a microwave oven.
claims.speaker: Davide Andrea
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea

claims.claim_text: Flat flexible cable, flexible printed circuit and conductive ink circuit are distinct technologies and none of them is a ribbon cable, which specifically denotes the multi-conductor cable terminated with IDC connectors.
claims.quote_verbatim: please don't call it ribbon cable, because a ribbon cable is a very specific thing
claims.speaker: Davide Andrea
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea

claims.claim_text: Rigid-flex construction can go well beyond the familiar two-layer flex board, placing multilayer rigid sections on top of the flexible core.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm talking about rigid on top of flex
claims.speaker: Zachariah Peterson
